producer_report.summary: Read requests now stay in `athena plan` and in the drain's queue. Root cause: `steward::queued_work` listed only jobs in state Queued, and reading a request moves it to Proposed. So after a plan read requests, they dropped out of the plan and the drain. `queued_work` now also lists Proposed jobs on the drained channels (steward and `cli`) with `read: true`. It leaves out Declined, Dispatched, Blocked and Closed jobs, other channels, and jobs a work decision approved (those are already listed by `approved_work`). `QueuedWork` gained a `read` field, and `RealSteps::queue` passes it on as `Item.read`, so the drain runs a read request without reading it again. The doc comment of `queued_work`, the module text of drain.rs, the README and CHANGELOG describe the new rule. The README sentence "it is no longer queued" for refused requests was no longer true, so I changed it. The misleading test now reads the job first (via `plan`) before checking its plan. `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all` all exited cleanly. I did not read the full test output, so I did not count tests or look at per-test results. The `--budget 2` "read none" remark was not investigated; I left it alone, as the accepted reading allowed.

criteria_check.criterion: A test queues requests on a drained channel, runs `plan` with a budget that reads some of them (stub reader), and then shows that the read requests are still in the plan entries and in `queue()` with read=true. Run `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: requests_read_by_plan_stay_in_the_plan_and_the_queue_and_a_second_plan_lists_them_again in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. It queues three requests on the cli channel and runs `drain::plan(&steps, 50.0)`, which reads them with the fake reader. It then asserts that the two read ones are Proposed, are in report.entries, and are in `steps.queue().items` with read=true. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain. That run passed 7 of 7 filtered tests before the final `cargo fmt` and `cargo test --locked`; the final full run exited 0.

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows that after a plan that reads requests, `drain` still works them: they are in its queue, are not read a second time, and are run in plan order. Run `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: drain_works_requests_a_plan_has_read_without_reading_them_again runs the real steps: after `plan` reads the request, `drain` lands it and the reader count stays 1. drain_runs_plan_read_items_in_plan_order_and_reads_none_of_them_again uses the stub with read_items a, b, c: the log has no 'read' entry and the runs are c, a, b.

criteria_check.criterion: A second `plan` after the first one reads requests prints the same open requests, not 'nothing is open'. The test checks this with the stub-backed plan output.
criteria_check.evidence: The first test above runs `plan` a second time. It asserts that the same two requests are listed, that the reader is not called again, and that `display::plan` does not contain 'nothing is open'. It uses the fake-agent-backed real steps rather than the `Stub` struct. The declined request is not listed the second time, but the first plan's report still shows it, because the first plan's entries are taken before its reads.

criteria_check.criterion: Read requests on channels other than the drained ones, jobs that are running or closed, and declined jobs do not enter the queue. A test covers each. `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
criteria_check.evidence: Declined: a real declined request ('make it better') is Declined after the plan and is absent from the queue (requests_read_by_plan_stay... test). Running, closed and declined states: `waits_for_drain` is asserted to return None for Declined, Dispatched, Blocked and Closed in steward::tests::only_queued_and_proposed_jobs_wait_for_the_drain_and_only_proposed_ones_are_read. Other channel and closed: the existing unit test unread_steward_and_cli_requests_are_queued_work_oldest_first still covers the 'web' channel and a closed job. There is no end-to-end test of a running (Dispatched) job's absence, and no unit test of a read request on a non-drained channel; those rest on the state function plus the channel filter. clippy and fmt ran clean.

criteria_check.criterion: The misleading test name `the_plan_of_a_read_job_names_a_missing_path_and_an_unresolved_referenced_job` in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs is replaced or backed by a test that really reads the job before checking its plan.
criteria_check.evidence: That test now sets a scenario reading, runs `drain::plan(&steps, 50.0)`, asserts the job has one reading, then checks the queue items are read and the plan's open questions.

criteria_check.criterion: The doc comment of `queued_work` and the module text of drain.rs describe the new rule: read requests stay queued for the drain until they run or close.
criteria_check.evidence: The doc comment on `queued_work` in crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs and the new bullet 'Read requests stay queued' in the module docs of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs.

open_issues: I did not investigate the 'default --budget 2 read none' symptom. It would be harmless now that unread requests stay queued; if the room check at budget 2 is wrong, that is a separate fix.

A request that was read and then refused for an incomplete plan (state Proposed) now stays in the queue and is reported as refused on every plan or drain, until the user corrects or closes it. That follows from the request, but it changes what the output shows.
mistakes: My first draft of the second-plan assertion compared the second plan's entries with the first plan's, which includes the declined request; I corrected it.
learnings: JobState is derived in store.rs `JobRecords::state`: no readings and no invocations is Queued; a latest reading with no capability is Declined; otherwise Proposed.
The plan report's `entries` come from the queue as it stood before the pass read anything, so a request the pass reads and finds declined is still listed in that first report.
The plan adds CHANGELOG.md as an extra touched path that does not exist at the base commit, so open-question assertions in tests should check for containment, not equality.
